title: OmniSpace: Efficient Geometry Awareness for Autonomous Vehicles MLLMs
claim: Prior approaches either ignore geometry or depend on costly external 3D models at inference; ours injects geometry cheaply with low inference complexity.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, (a)/(b)/(c) with summary comparison table under each
description: Three side-by-side boxed panels compare paradigms for autonomous-driving MLLMs. (a) 2D MLLM: multi-view images and an instruction feed an MLLM, and the output list shows red crosses for geometric conditioning, cross-view reasoning and 3D prior injection, with low inference complexity. (b) 2D MLLM plus an external frozen 3D model, marked with a snowflake. It feeds the MLLM, so all three rows read External, and inference complexity is High in red. (c) Our approach: images, instruction and a camera-pose diagram with colored frustums feed the OmniSpace block. That block holds a Camera Pose Injector and Multi-view Epipolar Attention. A dotted line sends images to the external 3D model, used only for distillation. Its rows read Plucker rays, Epipolar attention and 3D distill., with Low complexity in green. Pastel greens and purples, with red and green for bad and good.
caption: Comparison between existing paradigms and \model.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable performance on 2D visual tasks, yet enhancing their spatial intelligence for real-world applications such as Autonomous Vehicles (AV) remains an open challenge. Existing geometry-aware MLLMs typically rely on auxiliary 3D models at inference time, introducing pipeline complexity and the risk of cascading failures. In this paper, we present OmniSpace, a simple yet effective plug-and-play paradigm for geometry-aware spatial reasoning from purely 2D observations. Motivated by our finding that current MLLMs are bottlenecked by weak cross-view correspondence and depth estimation, OmniSpace introduces a Camera Pose Injector, a Multi-view Epipolar Attention module, and a 3D Geometric Distillation objective that jointly address these two limitations by transferring geometric knowledge into the model. Extensive experiments show that OmniSpace surpasses existing methods on planning benchmarks (nuScenes, Bench2Drive), risk detection (nuInstruct), language (Omnidrive), and generalization (DriveBench).
